clue.text: Pass cost United a thrashing

indicators.note: a thrashing knocks things about, so the letters of cost, United and a are beaten into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A football report: a defeat has cost Manchester United dearly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a thrashing' is the anagram signal, and its own A belongs to the fodder: COST + UNITED + A gives eleven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass a rival in a race is to get ahead and leave them behind, which is a synonym.

clue.text: Last of ormolu trim left on plate

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter, here the end of ormolu

parts.note: to trim something is to tidy it, to neaten it

explanation.surface: A gilded ormolu trim lies uneaten on a decorative plate.
explanation.walkthrough: Ormolu is gilded bronze used to decorate furniture and plates, which makes 'plate' look like dinnerware or metalwork.
explanation.definitionFit: Food still left on the plate at the end of a meal has not been consumed.

clue.text: Alluring birds with ale, drunk and on Ecstasy

indicators.note: drunk describes the birds and ale as tipsy, so their letters reel into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
E is the street abbreviation for the drug Ecstasy

explanation.surface: Women (birds, in British slang) made alluring by drink and drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'birds' is British slang for young women, which suits the party picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Something alluring is attractive and worth wanting, a synonym.

clue.text: With no parking, stay in charge of patient

indicators.note: with no says the letter for parking is dropped from the word for stay

parts.note: to stay somewhere briefly is to stop there
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A hospital official ruling that a patient may stay but without a parking space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'patient' looks like a hospital noun; here it is the adjective, uncomplaining in hardship.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoic person endures pain and trouble without complaint, so is patient in the enduring sense.

clue.text: Relevant support in Apple's first operating system

indicators.note: in places the word for support inside the other letters
Apple's first is the opening letter of the word Apple

parts.note: a prop is a support

explanation.surface: A tech note about relevant support built into Apple's first operating system.
explanation.definitionFit: Apropos means pertinent or to the point, a synonym of relevant.

clue.text: Falls about when about half dead

parts.note: C, from circa, means about
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
CA, short for circa, also means about

indicators.note: half of the four-letter word dead is its first two letters

explanation.surface: Someone falls down and is found about half dead.
explanation.walkthrough: The two 'about's give different abbreviations of circa, C then CA.
explanation.definitionFit: A cascade is a waterfall, and falls is another name for a waterfall.

clue.text: Doctor to pose with chest instrument

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are altered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A doctor asks a patient to pose so the chest can be examined with an instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' reads as a physician but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The listening device a physician uses on the chest is a medical instrument.

clue.text: Voyage for ships' companies, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word for ships' companies is spoken, giving one that sounds alike

parts.note: a ship's company is its crew, so ships' companies are crews

explanation.surface: Talk of a voyage put on for shipping firms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'companies' looks like businesses, but a ship's company is the people aboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A cruise is a pleasure voyage at sea, an example of a voyage.

clue.text: You French scoff over large dishes

parts.note: tu is the French familiar word for you

indicators.note: over says the word for scoff is turned round

parts.note: to scoff is to jeer or sneer

explanation.surface: A French diner scoffing a meal served in large dishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scoff' suggests eating greedily; here it means to mock.
explanation.definitionFit: Tureens are deep lidded serving bowls, an example of large dishes for soup.

clue.text: Ship so overturned by man-eating monster

indicators.note: overturned says the word for so is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: ergo is Latin for therefore, so
SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: A ship capsized by a sea monster that eats men.
explanation.definitionFit: In fairy tales a female ogre is a giant monster that devours people.

clue.text: Lay out one on door search

parts.note: to lay out money is to spend or invest it
I is the Roman numeral one
a gate is a kind of door

explanation.surface: Instructions to spend money on a door search.
explanation.definitionFit: To investigate is to examine or search into something, a synonym of search as a verb.

clue.text: One cheats in party game

definitions.meaning: a swindler or crook, someone who cheats people
the game where players contort themselves on a mat of coloured spots

explanation.walkthrough: Twister is a well-known party game played on a spotted mat.
explanation.definitionFit: A twister is a dishonest person who twists the truth, and the name of a game.

clue.text: Officer roughly put leader of terrorists in torment

parts.note: CA, short for circa, means roughly

indicators.note: in places the letter inside the word for torment

parts.note: pain is torment

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An officer put the terrorist leader through rough torment.
explanation.definitionFit: A captain is a commissioned officer in the army or navy.

clue.text: Once capsized crossing a body of water

indicators.note: crossing means the jumbled letters straddle the a, holding it inside
capsized says the letters of once are overturned and jumbled

explanation.surface: A boat once capsized while crossing a stretch of water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capsized' turns ONCE into OCEN, and 'crossing' puts A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocean is one of the great seas, the largest kind of body of water.

clue.text: Money that is admitting Queen supporter

parts.note: brass is British slang for money

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the letters for Queen go inside

parts.note: IE, id est, means that is
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: Money admitting someone to a royal fan club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporter' suggests a royalist fan; it is an undergarment.
explanation.definitionFit: A bra holds up and supports the bust, so is jokingly a supporter.

clue.text: A terrific oily mechanic

indicators.note: oily suggests something slippery that slides about, so the letters slither into a new order

explanation.surface: Praise for a terrific mechanic covered in oil.
explanation.definitionFit: An artificer is a skilled craftsman, especially a military or naval mechanic.

clue.text: Most macabre secret unfolded about meat dish?

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the word for meat dish
unfolded says the word secret is opened out and rearranged

parts.note: a pie is a meat dish

explanation.surface: A grisly secret revealed about what went into a meat pie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfolded' rearranges the six letters of 'secret' round the dish; the surface recalls the grim London tale of Sweeney Todd's pies.
explanation.definitionFit: Creepiest means most eerie and unsettling, close to most macabre.

clue.text: Teach English University course beginning in time

indicators.note: in places the following letters inside the word for time

parts.note: a date is a point in time

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Teaching an English course at university that begins on time.
explanation.definitionFit: To educate someone is to instruct them, a synonym of teach.

clue.text: Plant with unpleasant odour produces fake medicine

parts.note: to plant something is to place it
BO is body odour

explanation.surface: A smelly plant yields a quack's fake remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like vegetation; here it is the verb, to put in position.
explanation.definitionFit: A placebo is a dummy pill with no active drug, a sham treatment.

clue.text: Dull sandwich has a French filling

indicators.note: filling means the French article goes inside the sandwich, like its filling

parts.note: a BLT is a bacon, lettuce and tomato sandwich
un is French for a

explanation.surface: A dull sandwich with a French filling.
explanation.definitionFit: Blunt describes an edge that is not sharp, which is a synonym of dull.

clue.text: Aristocrat, apart from old lace

parts.note: bar means except, apart from
lace is an open net fabric

explanation.surface: An aristocrat with nothing but old lace to his name.
explanation.definitionFit: A baronet holds a hereditary British title just below a baron, so is a minor aristocrat.

clue.text: Top mark in German?

parts.note: seems to be a top grade in a German exam, but it is the mark sitting on top of German vowels

explanation.walkthrough: The two dots placed over a, o or u in German are a mark written on top of a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: This diacritic is literally a mark above letters in German spelling, the reading the question hints at.

clue.text: Span on prize bird's feathers

indicators.note: on in an across clue puts the word for span after the word for prize

parts.note: a plum is a prize job or reward
a span of time can be an age

explanation.surface: Measuring the wingspan of a prize-winning bird's feathers.
explanation.definitionFit: Plumage is the whole coat of feathers covering a bird.

clue.text: Stops losing head and relaxes

indicators.note: losing head means the first letter is dropped from the word for stops

parts.note: ceases means stops

explanation.surface: Someone stops losing their head and calms down.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease off is to loosen or relax, so eases matches relaxes.

clue.text: Part of calf or elegant part of limb

indicators.note: part of says the letters are found within the words calf or elegant

explanation.surface: Anatomy notes on a calf, or an elegant section of the leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'calf' misleads twice: it is a leg muscle or a young cow, while the answer hides across 'calf or elegant'.
explanation.definitionFit: A foreleg is a front leg of an animal, the front section of its limbs.

clue.text: Stroke initially soothing after worries

indicators.note: after says the soothing letter comes behind the word for worries

parts.note: cares are worries

indicators.note: initially means take the opening letter of soothing

explanation.surface: A soothing stroke given after troubles.
explanation.definitionFit: To caress is to stroke gently and affectionately, a synonym.

clue.text: Show criminal's almost expected before court …

indicators.note: before puts the criminal ahead of the other pieces

parts.note: a con, short for convict, is a criminal; the 's is a link

indicators.note: almost means the word for expected loses its last letter

parts.note: due means expected, as in a train due at six

explanation.surface: A criminal's court appearance, his show due shortly.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs this clue into the next; 'Show' here is the verb, to guide someone round.
explanation.definitionFit: To conduct visitors round a house is to show or guide them, a synonym.

clue.text: … villain's given time by judge for show

parts.note: a demon is a villain, and villain's supplies demon plus S
to rate something is to judge its value

explanation.surface: Continuing the story: the villain sentenced by a judge as an example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given time' sounds like a prison sentence, but it just adds T.
explanation.definitionFit: To demonstrate something is to display or exhibit it, a synonym of show.
